attributes.residual: THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE KEEP, and the reason P1 was thrown away despite being the mandated lever and despite being BETTER on both arbiters. At real 474 (P1+P3) wf_word_diff reported 'RELOC-SYMBOL MISMATCH: 2 instruction(s) whose WORD is identical in both streams relocate a DIFFERENT symbol -- +0x000c target lbl_80116450 ours lbl_80127DE8; +0x001c target lbl_80127DE8 ours lbl_80116450'. The baseline had zero. P1 transposes the two initialised pointers, so it transposes their two @lo/@ha materialisations, and at 0x0c and 0x1c our stream now relocates the OTHER symbol behind an identical instruction word. The code stays semantically correct -- each variable still gets its own address -- but the relocation CORRESPONDENCE is broken, and that is invisible to real, to fuzzy, to the multiset and to the differing-word count alike (claim.law.SA_...20260902.v1). It is also disqualifying for the postprocessor path: a copy_register_fields rule over that state would reproduce the target text with two relocations bound to the wrong atoms, exactly the hazard claim.law.HV_permute-payload-check-does-not-bind-a-relocation-to-its-atom.20260901.v1 records. The isolation probe P6 shows the two effects separate cleanly: P3 alone is -24 real, +0.2309 local fuzzy AND reloc-clean, while P1's extra -10 real is bought with the two mismatched rows. -10 real is not worth a relocation defect no score can ever report. THE WITHHELD RULE, proved and deliberately not shipped. A three-stage composition closes fn_800C03E0 completely and was run through the real apply_patch against the extracted retail object twice -- on the pre-source-work bytes ('BYTE-EQUAL; 220 word(s) changed') and again on the KEPT bytes ('BYTE-EQUAL; 206 word(s) changed'), both with the datum screen at FULL strength reading orig/GUNE5D/sys/main.dol. COUNT PARITY, the deciding fact for postprocessor candidacy: 433/433 instructions (ours/target), unchanged across every probe in this record. It is: instruction_permutation [{start 0x3cc, end 0x3d8, order [2,0,1], before_sha256 821c10da07262fe6fef891490e3c3af2f6071251f93ca3fba0098a39c7bb3753, after_sha256 0bfef4e0d3216d10afdf2ef87e9b8976e53b17c5551443ebce9e62d364d6210b, both relocation hashes the empty-string hash e3b0c442... since the window is relocation-free in both objects}] + equivalent_copy_form [{at 0x3cc, proof constant_dataflow_recolor, our_source 18}] + copy_register_fields true, audit permuted_instructions 3. WHY THE PERMUTATION IS THERE: the target initialises four zero webs at 0x3c8..0x3d4 and we initialise ours in a different ORDER, so the use at +0x3d8 (`addi r0,r16,12` against ours `addi r0,r20,12`) makes the running renaming two-valued -- copy_register_fields alone REFUSES with '+0x3cc: base register presence differs (g0 vs g19)' and the form stage alone gets one step further and REFUSES with '+0x3d8: use of g20 does not correspond to g16 under the running renaming'. Rotating our three definitions [2,0,1] restores the correspondence, which is the TowerCheckMessages recolor-repair device at a new site. WHY IT IS WITHHELD: the Mandatory-policy bar is a parked or capped record with literal probed_form axes, and this function's newest record explicitly says the recolor axis 'was never probed as a source problem this run' -- and when it finally was, this session, it moved 24 real in two probes. Shipping a rule now would (a) create the fifteenth unprovenanced rule in the same run this lane spent repairing fourteen, and (b) SOURCE-FREEZE dbgtext.c at fn_800C03E0 under claim.law.webfrank-pinned-function-source-freeze.20260831.v1, converting a live and paying axis into a frozen EQUIVALENT. Provenance first, per the run-48 withhold precedent. The hashes above are bound to commit d46124aea and must be re-derived after any further source movement; the shape (window, order, proof mode, our_source) is what transfers. NOTE ON THE INHERITED DESCRIPTION: the work order and the previous record both call this residual 'pure REGFIELD-ONLY, 216 words, multiset IDENTICAL'. wf_word_diff does read 'REGFIELD-ONLY 216 ... OPCODE 0' -- and fndiff --ops reads 'multiset DIFFERS, target-only +1 addi, ours-only -1 li' on the SAME bytes. Both are right and the discrepancy is mnemonic aliasing: `li rD,K` IS `addi rD,r0,K`, so the two words share a primary opcode and differ in the rA field, which the word decoder scores as a register field. But rA=0 in a d-form slot is the literal zero, NOT GPR 0, so no copy_register_fields rule may rewrite it -- claim.law.WP_the-ra-zero-flag-belongs-to-the-field-not-to-the-position-a-value-lands-in.20260903.v1 -- and the guard says so in exactly those words ('base register presence differs (g0 vs g19)'). A 'pure REGFIELD-ONLY' reading of this function is therefore literally true at the bit level and wrong about candidacy, which is the same shape as claim.law.HV_lexical-regfield-test-shadows-the-copy-form-arrow-for-mr-versus-li.20260901.v1.

hypothesis.statement: The initialised-pointer class is the live lever and it is NOT exhausted: swapping `fmts` and `tblB` moved real 508->498 but BROKE the relocation-symbol correspondence, and swapping `qline` and `line` moved 508->484 cleanly. The next lane's step 1 is to find a form that buys the fmts colour WITHOUT reordering the two @lo materialisations -- the target defines fmts at `@0x20 addi r26,r4,0` (ADDR16_LO of lbl_80116450) while ours defines it at `@0x20 addi r28,r4,0` on the same symbol, and tblA agrees in both streams at `@0x18 addi r27,r3,0` (lbl_802C45CC), so the target's fmts web sits BELOW tblA's r27 while ours sits above it -- the target's fmts is losing a contention to a `li 20` web (target `@0x50 li r29,20` against ours `@0x50 li r30,20`) rather than sitting where declaration order would put it. Attack the LIFETIME, not the order: savedregs reports 3 live ranges escaped to a volatile and 1 volatile role promoted in ours, the promoted one being the web our stream defines at `@0x7c li r22,0` where the target's corresponding web is `@0x7c li r16,0` inside the callee-saved range r16-r31; our build is spending a callee-saved register on a range the target keeps volatile, and that is what shifts every colour below it.
